trips.route_note: Take the direct CP Sintra line from Lisbon's Rossio station; the historic centre and Pena Palace are a short local bus or tuk-tuk ride uphill from Sintra station.
trips.why: Direct CP train from Rossio is fast and frequent, with the centre and Pena Palace reachable by short local bus or tuk-tuk uphill.
know: Pena Palace requires timed tickets booked ahead in high season
Weekdays are far less crowded than weekends
Palaces and gardens can be chilly and misty even in summer

trips.route_note: Take the direct CP suburban train from Lisbon's Cais do Sodré station to Cascais, about 40 minutes along the coast.
trips.why: Direct coastal CP train from Cais do Sodré is quicker and cheaper than the bus and drops you in the town centre.
know: The coastal train ride itself is scenic, so sit on the sea side
Boca do Inferno and the old town are an easy walk from the station
Summer weekends get very busy at the beaches

trips.route_note: Direct Alfa Pendular and Intercidades trains run to Coimbra-B, then a short shuttle train or taxi to the university and old town.
trips.why: The train takes 1h 36m, is the fastest option, and runs direct to Coimbra-B, with a short shuttle or taxi to the old town.
know: Coimbra-B is outside the old town, so allow time for the shuttle train or taxi to the university.
Direct trains run from Lisboa Oriente; daily frequency isn't listed, so check timetables before you go.

trips.route_note: Take the CP Sintra line from Rossio to Queluz-Belas station, then walk about ten minutes to the palace.
trips.tour_query: Queluz Palace half day from Lisbon
trips.why: CP Sintra line reaches Queluz-Belas in 17 minutes, far faster than the 1h05 bus, with a ten-minute walk to the palace.
know: The palace interior is visited by guided tour only
Check opening days, as it closes on some weekdays
Combine with Sintra since it is on the same train line

bus.via: Gare do Oriente 21-C to Avenida Dom João II

trips.route_note: Take a direct Fertagus train from Lisbon's Roma-Areeiro or Entrecampos station to Setúbal, about an hour.
trips.why: The bus is faster than the train here and still direct, though the train is a simple one-seat ride.
know: Boat trips to see dolphins in the Sado estuary are the main draw
Fresh fish restaurants downtown are a local highlight
The Fertagus train crosses the river and is a scenic alternative
